The feature is done and committed as `62a5d97` on `run/e1-a1/a`. Nothing is pushed, and no server was started. The gate passes: `yarn architecture gate --base a4d6621016f6dd261ce851c6d2e69180afecab61 --mode architecture` reports PASS on every step. The storm is marked `done: true`, and the code carries exactly what it names.

**What I built**

- **Architecture first.** The storm's gate failure was two undeclared contexts. I declared `Accounts` and `Notes` in `conventions/typescript.yaml` and described them in `conventions/domain.yaml`, with no relationship between them, since Notes takes the owner from the caller. That is recorded in `docs/adr/0001-accounts-and-notes-contexts.md`. I also wrote `docs/adr/0002-sign-in-is-an-application-service.md`, which explains why login is not a command or query.
- **Accounts:** sign-up is a command, sign-in is an application service that answers a token, and `GET /accounts/me` reads the caller's own account. Passwords are hashed with `bcryptjs` and tokens are signed with `jose` (HS256), both behind ports. The token is read from `Authorization: Bearer`, and a bad token makes the request anonymous.
- **Notes:** create, edit, archive and restore are commands; list and read are queries. Ownership, archive rules and the 100-character title rule live in the aggregate.
- **Tests:** 96 unit tests across 21 suites and 13 end-to-end tests over HTTP. Format, lint and typecheck are clean.

**Decisions I made where the spec was silent**

- Every note route answers 403 synchronously to an anonymous caller, before anything is accepted. The spec only stated this for `POST /notes`, `GET /notes` and `GET /notes/{id}`, and I applied it to edit, archive and restore too.
- Another account's note is a 404 to read. To change it, the command is accepted (202) and its outcome is an `ERROR` with `NotNoteOwner`. I did not make that a 404 because the outcome model has no 404.
- Sign-in is `POST /accounts/login`. The grammar's `read` verb is `GET`, so this is a deliberate exception, documented in ADR 0002.
- I dropped the swagger `tags` from the new routes, because `@fastify/swagger` is not installed and the typed route options reject them.

**What is unclear or open**

- **Token secret.** Tokens are signed with `TOKEN_SECRET` when it is set. Otherwise a random secret is drawn at start, so every token dies on restart. Set `TOKEN_SECRET` in any real deployment.
- **Sign-in timing.** An unknown email returns faster than a wrong password, because bcrypt is skipped. The answer text is identical, but the timing is not.
- **Sign-up reveals existence.** A duplicate sign-up says the email is in use. That is normal for sign-up, but it is a choice.
- **Email uniqueness under concurrency.** The in-memory store enforces uniqueness in the same step as the write, which is what a unique index would do. A real database needs that index.

Feature 2 is done and committed as `439a47b` on `run/e1-a1/a`. Nothing is pushed, and no server was started. The gate passes against `133959efb3019456bb524c2a6ced2198ac5b5c9c` in architecture mode, and the storm `pin-a-note` is marked `done: true` with the code carrying all of it.

**What I built**

- **Commands:** `PinNote` and `UnpinNote` are on the `Note` aggregate, with `POST /notes/{id}/pin` and `POST /notes/{id}/unpin`. Each answers 202 and records `NotePinned` or `NoteUnpinned`. Anonymous callers get a synchronous 403, as on the other note routes.
- **Rules:** a second pin and an unpin of an unpinned note are refused. Pinning an archived note is refused. Archiving leaves the pin in place, and an archived note can still be unpinned. Only the owner can pin or unpin.
- **Reads:** `GET /notes` and `GET /notes/{id}` now include `pinned`. The list is ordered pinned first, then most recent first within each group. The ordering is part of the query port's contract.
- **Tests:** 99 unit tests and 17 end-to-end tests pass. Typecheck, lint, format and the conventions check are clean.

**Decisions I made**

- No architecture change and no ADR. The storm stays inside `Notes`, so no context or relationship is new.
- The "pinned first" ordering is applied in the in-memory query adapter, because that is where this application keeps its read side. A database adapter would need to keep the same order.
- The refusal for pinning an archived note has its own type, `ArchivedNoteCannotBePinned`, so its message says what to do instead of reusing the edit-refusal wording.

**What is unclear**

- The spec does not say which refusal wins when a note is both archived and already pinned. I check for archived first, so pinning an archived note that is already pinned answers `ArchivedNoteCannotBePinned`.

Feature 3 is done and committed as `8679ef4` on `run/e1-a1`. Nothing is pushed, and no server was started. The gate passes against `30de931f5c16abe7afefefe58adea70c817520d8` in architecture mode, and `tag-a-note` is marked `done: true`. The code carries all four storm items.

**What I built**

- **Tags:** the `Tag` value object accepts one lowercase word of 1 to 30 characters, drawn from a–z, 0–9 and hyphens. Anything else is refused and never rewritten.
- **Commands:** `TagNote` and `UntagNote` are on the `Note` aggregate. They are served by `POST /notes/{id}/tags` and `DELETE /notes/{id}/tags/{tag}`, and they answer 202 and record `NoteTagged` and `NoteUntagged`.
- **Rules:** a repeated tag, an untag of a missing tag, an eleventh tag, and any change to an archived note are refusals. A note keeps its tags through archive and restore.
- **Reads:** each note shows `tags` in the order they were added. `GET /notes?tag=` filters the owner's existing list and keeps its order, pinned first.
- **Tests:** 115 unit tests and 20 end-to-end tests pass. Typecheck, lint, format and the conventions check are clean.

**Decisions I made**

- No architecture change and no ADR, because the storm stays inside `Notes`.
- The tag filter lives on the existing `GetMyNotes` query, not on a new query. The storm lists no new queries, so that is the only shape that keeps the inventory exact.
- A filter value that is not a valid tag is not refused. It simply matches nothing and returns an empty list. The spec does not say, and I preferred a plain filter to a 400 error.
- A tag value is echoed back in the refusal's context. It is the caller's own input and never reaches the Tracker's records.

**What is unclear**

- The spec says the list is ordered "the same as their list", but it does not say what happens to ties. I kept the list's existing order: pinned first, then most recent first, with ties falling back to the store's order.

Feature 4 is done and committed as `46f94c9` on `run/e1-a1`. Nothing is pushed, and no server was started. The gate passes against `b2056c061294ddfe57a46a248a0c02acd7c0a36f` in architecture mode, and `share-a-note` is marked `done: true` with the code carrying all four items.

**Architecture first**

- The storm needed a relationship Notes did not have: Notes asks Accounts whether an account exists. I declared it in `conventions/domain.yaml` as an `owned-port` from Accounts to Notes, with `customer-supplier` and `anti-corruption-layer`. ADR 0003 records the decision.
- The declaration went in as `planned: true` while the code was not written. I removed the flag once the adapter existed. The conventions check accepts the relationship as carried.
- Notes owns the port `IAccountDirectory`. The adapter `AccountsReadModelDirectory` answers it over Accounts' read model. Accounts now exports its queries port from its wiring, which is the only way Notes reaches Accounts.

**The feature**

- **Sharing:** `ShareNote` is a command on the aggregate that records `NoteShared`. The domain service `NoteSharing` checks the account exists before the aggregate applies its own rules. Those rules are owner only, not archived, not twice, and not yourself.
- **Recipients:** an account a note is shared with can read it, and `GET /notes/shared` lists what is shared with it, most recent first, with `ownerId` on each item. It cannot edit, archive, restore, pin, tag or share.
- **Owner's view:** `GET /notes/{id}` gains `ownerId` for everyone who can read the note. The owner's answer also gains `sharedWith`.
- **Tests:** 119 unit tests and 25 end-to-end tests pass. Typecheck, lint, format and conventions are clean.

**Decisions I made**

- A recipient's view leaves out `pinned`, `tags` and `sharedWith`. Those are the owner's own organisation, so the recipient gets id, owner, title, text, archived and createdAt only.
- The owner's `sharedWith` lists account ids only, as the spec says.
- The directory check runs before the aggregate's rules. A share with an unknown account therefore reports `RecipientNotFound` even when the note is also archived.
- `ownerId` is on every note response, not only the detail view. It is the same schema for each route, and a client ignores fields it does not know.

**What is unclear**

- The spec does not say whether the owner's detail view should list `sharedWith` in a particular order. I return the order the note was shared in.
- The spec does not say whether sharing is one way or whether a recipient can share further. The storm says nothing beyond "nothing else", so the recipient cannot share.
- `GET /notes` does not list notes shared with the caller. Only `GET /notes/shared` does. The spec keeps the two lists separate, so I did not merge them.

Feature 5 is done and committed as `cfe96e5` on `run/e1-a1`. Nothing is pushed, and no server was started. The gate passes against `77a4dcec02b51b66da87feadf4c5855717ae7a4d` in architecture mode, and `notify-on-archive` is marked `done: true`.

**Architecture first**

- **New context `Notifications`**, declared in the binding and the domain map under a supporting subdomain. ADR 0004 records it.
- **Relationship `Notes → Notifications`** over the integration event `NoteArchived`, with `published-language` and `anti-corruption-layer`. I declared it `planned` while the code was not written, then removed the flag once the code carried it. The contract lives in `SharedKernel/Application/IntegrationEvents`, the only place contracts between contexts live.

**The feature**

- **Notes** records `NoteArchived` with the owner, the title, the archiving time, and the accounts the note was shared with at that moment. Its handler publishes the integration event through the outbox after the commit.
- **Notifications** translates that event in an anti-corruption handler, writing one notification per recipient. The owner is skipped. A note shared with nobody writes nothing. Each archiving writes its own notification.
- **`GET /notifications`** lists the caller's notifications, most recent first, with exactly `id`, `kind`, `noteId`, `noteTitle` and `archivedAt`. Anonymous callers get 403, and nobody sees another person's list.
- **Tests:** 123 unit tests and 28 end-to-end tests pass. Lint, format, typecheck and conventions are clean.

**A bug from feature 1, fixed here**

The gate's end-to-end run failed once on an accounts test. The test logged in right after the 202 for sign-up, without waiting for the sign-up outcome. The product is correct: the account exists only once the operation succeeds. I changed the two tests to wait for the outcome, and the suite has been stable over several runs since. The amended commit includes that fix.

**Decisions I made**

- The owner's archive event carries the recipients at that moment, so a later share or unshare cannot change who was told.
- The owner is filtered out in the Notifications handler as well as in Notes, so the hot spot holds even if a future sharing rule breaks.
- Notifications are written once and never changed. There is no repository lookup by id, because nothing needs one yet.

**What is unclear**

- The spec does not say how an `archivedAt` tie is ordered between two notifications from the same instant. I kept insertion order, newest first.
- The spec does not say whether the list should include a notification for a note that was later unshared. Nothing unshares yet, so I did not decide that.

Feature 6 is done and committed as `ca21cea` on `run/e1-a1`. Nothing is pushed, and no server was started. The gate passes against `3c146e1e1c29c33e6d85cd73a087771069b93220` in architecture mode, and `plan-and-quota` is marked `done: true` with the code carrying all four items.

**Architecture first**

- **New context `Plans`**, declared in the binding and the domain map under a supporting subdomain. ADR 0005 records it.
- **Relationship `Plans → Notes`** as an owned port, with `customer-supplier` and `anti-corruption-layer`. Notes owns `IPlanLimits`, and the adapter `PlansReadModelLimits` reads Plans' read model, wired from Plans' exported queries port. As before, I declared it `planned` while writing the code and removed the flag once the code carried it.

**The feature**

- **Plans:** everyone starts on Free, which is the default and records nothing. `PUT /plans/me` switches the plan and records `PlanChanged`. `GET /plans/me` returns `{ plan, noteLimit }`, which is 10 on Free and null on Unlimited.
- **Quota:** `NoteWriting`, a domain service in Notes, asks the limit through the port and counts the owner's notes through the repository. Archived notes count. The eleventh note on Free is refused as an `ERROR` outcome. A plan that went back to Free over the limit keeps its notes and refuses only new ones.
- **Tests:** 130 unit tests and 32 end-to-end tests pass. Typecheck, lint, format and conventions are clean.

**Decisions I made**

- **A plan name that is neither free nor unlimited** is refused by the route with a 400, because the schema enumerates the two names. The domain still refuses unknown names too, and a unit test covers that. The spec does not say which refusal form applies, and this is the one I chose.
- **Switching to the plan already in use** is refused as an `AlreadyOnPlan` outcome. This follows the pattern of pinning twice, and the spec is silent on it.
- **The quota check and the count are not serialised.** Two writes at once could both see nine notes and both pass. The in-memory application runs in one process and does not interleave them, so the tests cannot show the race. ADR 0005 records it as the thing a database adapter must guarantee.

**What is unclear**

- The spec does not say what happens if a person changes plan while a note write is already in flight. I treated each command as atomic, which is what the in-memory store gives.
- The spec does not say whether the limit should be checked against notes shared with the person. Only owned notes count, as the storm says.

Feature 7 is done and committed as `94f323c` on `run/e1-a1`. Nothing is pushed, and no server was started. The gate passes against `c9a402db542d45631ae3a7aa6c415a7282849aee` in architecture mode, and `remind-a-note` is marked `done: true` with the code carrying all of it.

**Architecture**

The relationship `Notes → Notifications` already existed from feature 5, so the new integration events are read as contracts on it and no relationship was added. I recorded the design in ADR 0006, since a newcomer would question it: no scheduler, and a reminder is shown when the list is read.

**What the feature does**

- **Notes** keeps one reminder per note. Scheduling again cancels a reminder still ahead, and archiving does the same. A reminder whose moment has come is kept, so its owner's notice stays. A moment in the past, an archived note, and a stranger are refused. `GET /notes/{id}` shows `remindAt`, or `null`.
- **Notifications** records each reminder fact as it arrives: scheduled, or cancelled. Facts are only ever added, so they settle in any order. When the list is read, a reminder shows once its moment has come, unless a cancellation was recorded for it. The shared accounts are never told.
- **`GET /notifications`** merges archivings and reminders, most recent first by each one's own moment. A reminder carries exactly `id`, `kind`, `noteId`, `noteTitle` and `remindAt`.
- **Tests:** 138 unit and 38 end-to-end tests pass. The timed flows passed three runs in a row.

**What I decided where the storm was silent**

- A reminder whose moment has come is kept when it is replaced, so the notice already shown stays in the list.
- The `remindAt` value is parsed in the handler, and an unparseable one is an `InvalidReminderTime` outcome. I did not test a value that fails the route's format check.
- Shown reminders are not compacted. The facts grow without bound, which ADR 0006 records as a later decision.
- `GET /notes` also carries `remindAt`, because it shares one response schema with the detail view.

**What is unclear**

- The spec says the list is "most recent first" but does not define how a reminder that was never read compares with an archiving. I used each one's own moment.
- A reminder is never shown to anyone who does not read the list after its moment. The storm chose that. A push or an email would need a scheduler, which is a separate architecture decision.
- The end-to-end reminder tests use real delays of a few hundred milliseconds to about a second, so a very slow machine could make them flaky.
